title: Native Random, Shape Morphs, Tategaki, Peek & Pop, Streaming Bubbles
description: Five patterns riding the platform's edge: native CSS random(), shape()-morphing heroes, vertical tategaki type, a peek-and-pop long-press, and the AI-era streaming bubble.

drops.title: Native Random Bursts
drops.description: Confetti, ember and bubble particle bursts driven by per-element custom properties, built for CSS's incoming native random() function.
drops.concept: CSS is gaining a random() function so each element can resolve its own randomized custom property directly in the stylesheet, with no JS math and no per-element inline styles. Since no stable browser ships it yet, this demo feature-detects support live via CSS.supports() and computes the same --dx/--dy/--rot/--dur custom properties in JS as a transparent fallback, consumed by the identical CSS keyframe either way.
drops.source: SitePoint — "CSS math-random() in Production: Native Randomness Without JavaScript"

interaction.mouse: Click anywhere on the stage to fire a confetti burst
interaction.click: Preset buttons trigger confetti, ember or bubble bursts
interaction.touch: Tap the stage or preset buttons

drops.title: Shape() Hero Morph
drops.description: Three hero panels liquify between organic curve outlines on hover using the new CSS shape() function.
drops.concept: CSS shape() brings native SVG-style path commands (line/curve/arc) to clip-path. Because the idle and hover states share the exact same command sequence — only coordinates differ — the browser can interpolate the whole outline continuously through a plain CSS transition, no SVG or JS animation loop required. A matched-vertex-count polygon() fallback keeps the same morph technique working in every browser today.
drops.source: web.dev — "New to the web platform, February 2026"

interaction.mouse: Hover a panel to morph its outline
interaction.click: Tap a panel to toggle the morphed state

drops.title: Tategaki Type Rails
drops.description: Vertical top-to-bottom headline columns with ruby glosses that slide into focus as you scroll sideways past them.
drops.concept: Traditional Japanese tategaki vertical typesetting — writing-mode: vertical-rl with text-orientation: mixed — turns each headline into a column read top-to-bottom, with a small <ruby>/<rt> gloss annotating it. An IntersectionObserver watches a horizontally scroll-snapping rail and adds an in-view class as each column crosses a visibility threshold, driving a blur-and-slide entrance purely through CSS transitions.

interaction.mouse: Scroll horizontally to move between rails

drops.title: Peek & Pop
drops.description: Press and hold a card — a radial progress ring fills at your touch point, then drag upward to pop into full detail.
drops.concept: A compound long-press gesture layered on Pointer Events: pointerdown starts a hold timer visualized as a filling SVG ring at the exact touch coordinates. Crossing the hold threshold triggers a 'peek' (short vibration, scrim, enlarged preview); dragging further upward past a second distance threshold 'pops' into a full detail overlay with a stronger vibration pattern. Releasing early at any stage cancels back to a plain tap — mirroring native mobile 3D-Touch-style compound gestures in vanilla JS.
drops.source: Muzli Design Blog — "What's Changing in Mobile App Design: UI Patterns That Matter in 2026"

interaction.mouse: Press and hold a card, drag up to pop, release to cancel
interaction.click: Short click registers a normal tap

drops.title: Streaming Response Bubble
drops.description: A token-by-token AI chat bubble with a blinking cursor, buffered code-fence reveal, and a live Stop control.
drops.concept: Response text is fed into a render queue action-by-action to simulate real SSE token streaming. Plain-text tokens append immediately with a blinking cursor, but content inside a fenced code block is buffered silently behind a 'writing code…' placeholder and only flushed as a highlighted <pre><code> block once the closing fence arrives — preventing any broken partial markup from flashing mid-stream. A Stop button halts the interval instantly, and copy/regenerate actions fade in only once the stream ends.

interaction.mouse: Click a preset to stream a response; Stop halts it mid-stream
interaction.click: Copy or Regenerate once streaming completes
